instruction.text: Which phrase can be removed from the second clause?

atoms.a: I enjoy paining landscapes and portraits, but my sister does not enjoy painting landscapes and portraits.

feedback.end:
Sometimes, too much repetition can actually reduce cohesion. In this example, removing the repeated phrase reduces the length of the sentence and makes it flow better. This is called ellipsis.

“I enjoy painting landscapes and portraits, but my sister does not.”

atoms.a: Daniel travels to his rugby training sessions by bus on Wednesday and Daniel travels to his rugby training sessions by bus on Saturday.

feedback.end: “Daniel travels to his rugby training sessions by bus on Wednesday and on Saturday.”

atoms.a: Javier would like to go swimming, but he isn’t allowed to go swimming.

feedback.end: “Javier would like to go swimming, but he isn’t allowed.”

instruction.text: Match the phrases to the sentences they have been removed from.

atoms.a: I know how to cook pasta, but my brother does not.
Rafael does not find exams stressful, but Julia does.
Tina enjoys reading and playing basketball.

trainers.instruction: Has the ellipsis in the sentence been used correctly?

atoms.a: Mo would like to go to Scotland over the summer, but Jackie would not.
Temi can drive a manual car, but Rob cannot drive a car.
Aaliyah goes to a British Sign Language night class every Monday and Thursday.
Maddy enjoys going to the cinema and Maddy enjoys writing poetry.
atoms.sound: Maddy enjoys going to the cinema and writing poetry.

atoms.a: Djamila likes red velvet cake,  but her brother does not like red velvet cake.
atoms.sound: Djamila likes red velvet cake, but her brother does not.

atoms.a: This restaurant serves lots of different vegetable dishes and this restaurant serves lots of different meat dishes.
atoms.sound: This restaurant serves lots of different vegetable and meat dishes.
